solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Homesick and lit up … continually lit up

indicators.note: lit up is slang for drunk, so these letters are reeling into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone feeling far from home gets drunk and then smokes one cigarette after another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lit up' appears twice: first as the slang for drunk that scrambles HOMESICK AND, then literally, as lighting cigarettes.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain-smoker lights each cigarette from the last, so smoking without a break is lighting up continually.

clue.text: No end to Scandinavian writings inspired by fish and cheese

indicators.note: inspired by means breathed in, so the writings go inside the fish

parts.note: char is a fish of the trout family

indicators.note: no end to means the last letter is removed

parts.note: the Eddas are Old Norse collections of poems and myths

explanation.surface: Norse texts, minus their ending, inspired a dish of fish and cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: The Eddas are medieval Icelandic collections of Norse myth and verse; 'inspired' is used in its literal sense of breathed in.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheddar is a hard English cheese, named after a village in Somerset.

clue.text: Was this when empire builder reduced American presence by 50%?

definitions.text: Was this when empire builder reduced American presence by 50%?

indicators.note: reduced means cut down, so letters are taken out of the emperor's name

parts.note: Augustus was the first Roman emperor, who built the empire

indicators.note: by 50% means only half of the American presence is taken away

parts.note: the name holds US, the American abbreviation, twice over

explanation.surface: A historical question: was this the month when the emperor halved the American presence?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the month really was named in honour of that emperor, so the whole clue doubles as its definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The eighth month was renamed in honour of the Roman emperor Augustus, so it is when he would be commemorated.

clue.text: He might mind his own blooming business!

definitions.text: He might mind his own blooming business!

parts.words: He might mind his own blooming business!
parts.note: blooming is a mild British oath, but here literal: a business full of flowers, minded by the one who grows them

explanation.surface: An exasperated retort: he ought to mind his own blooming business!
explanation.walkthrough: 'blooming' is a polite British substitute for a swear word; read literally it means flowering, so the business is raising plants.
explanation.definitionFit: A nurseryman runs a plant nursery, growing and selling flowers and shrubs as his trade.

clue.text: Mess about, backing away from mate

indicators.note: away from means taken off, so those letters leave the friend

parts.note: mucker is British slang for a friend or mate

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the word for about is read backwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: An instruction to fool around while edging away from a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mess about' looks like one phrase, but 'about' gives RE, reversed to ER and removed from MUCKER, a British slang word for a pal.
explanation.definitionFit: Muck is dirt or filth, and a mess is an untidy, dirty state.

clue.text: Man of Kent quaffing pink stuff, English — something refined

indicators.note: quaffing means drinking in, so the wine goes inside the man

parts.note: Ken is a man's name, and one that sits in Kent
rosé is pink wine

explanation.surface: A Kentish man downs a glass of rosé and something else English and classy.
explanation.walkthrough: A Man of Kent is a real term for someone born east of the River Medway, but here it only supplies a man's name; rosé loses its accent, as accents are ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Kerosene is paraffin oil, produced by refining crude petroleum.

clue.text: Promote a great number in plain clothes section of force

indicators.note: promote means move up, and in a down clue that reads the letters bottom to top
in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, whose British detectives work in plain clothes
many means a great number

explanation.surface: An order to promote many officers to the plain-clothes department of the police force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'force' looks like the police, but the definition is 'of force'. In a down clue, promoting moves letters upward, so they read from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Dynamic relates to forces producing motion, as in the physics of dynamics, so it means pertaining to energy.

clue.text: One getting even after losing face with German?

definitions.text: One getting even after losing face with German?

parts.note: one is the article a

indicators.note: losing face means the word even loses its front letter

parts.note: taken as written before its first letter goes

explanation.surface: Someone takes revenge after being humiliated in dealings with a German.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer while also building it: A, then EVEN without its first letter (VEN), then GER.
explanation.definitionFit: An avenger is a person who exacts revenge, settling a score by paying back a wrong.

clue.text: Determinations of revised means tests repeating conclusions and wasting time

indicators.note: revised means reworked, so the letters are rearranged
wasting means losing, so the time letter disappears
repeating says the endings of the two words are given a second time, added after them

parts.note: taken as written as the letters to rearrange
the conclusions of means and tests are both the letter S, here repeated as an extra pair

explanation.surface: Welfare assessments are rewritten, repeating their findings and wasting time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeating' says the endings of the two words, S and S, are given a second time; a T for time goes before everything is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Assessments are judgements or evaluations, the conclusions reached when something is determined.

clue.text: Long-lasting, elegant, and not, in retrospect, boring

indicators.note: boring into something means drilling inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: chic means stylish or elegant

indicators.note: looking back, so the word for and not is read in the other direction

parts.note: nor means and not

explanation.surface: A description of something enduring, stylish and, looking back, never dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' looks like the opposite of 'elegant' in a list of adjectives, but it means drilling into something.
explanation.definitionFit: Chronic describes a condition that persists for a long time, especially an illness.

clue.text: This vice girl, renouncing ecstasy, applied for social provisions

indicators.note: renouncing means giving up, so the drug's letter is taken from the fodder
applied means put to new use, so the remaining letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rework, taken as written
E is the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A former prostitute gave up drugs and applied for welfare.
explanation.walkthrough: Take E (ecstasy) from THIS VICE GIRL and rearrange the remaining letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Civil rights are the entitlements a society guarantees to its citizens, such as equality and free speech.

clue.text: Bypass is going round street engulfed by the sea

indicators.note: going round means turning back, so the word is is read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written before being turned

indicators.note: engulfed by means swallowed inside, so the street goes within the sea

parts.note: the deep is a poetic name for the sea

explanation.surface: A new road skirts round a street that has been flooded by the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' seems to describe the bypass circling a street, but it only turns the little word 'is' around; 'the deep' is a literary term for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidestep something is to avoid it by stepping around it, just as you bypass an obstacle.

clue.text: Author returning honour secured by credit card?

indicators.note: returning means the whole combination is read backwards
secured by means held inside, so the honour goes within the card

parts.note: Visa is a brand of credit card
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A writer is rewarded with an honour, but paid for it with plastic.
explanation.walkthrough: The Order of Merit is a British honour in the monarch's personal gift; the question mark marks the card as one example of credit.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Asimov was a prolific science-fiction writer, author of I, Robot and the Foundation novels.

clue.text: Dilapidated hut for sheep on Lancashire's borders

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
a shack is a crude hut

indicators.note: borders means the outermost letters, the first and last

parts.note: Lancashire, a county in north-west England

explanation.surface: A tumbledown sheep shelter on the edge of Lancashire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hut for sheep' gives RAM SHACK, and the borders of Lancashire (a county of north-west England) are L and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramshackle describes a building in a state of disrepair, falling apart.

clue.text: Belgrade resident envisaging strike, primarily from the east?

definitions.text: Belgrade resident envisaging strike, primarily from the east?

indicators.note: from the east means read from right to left, as on a map, so the order is reversed
primarily means taking the first letter of each of the four words

parts.note: first letter B
first letter R
first letter E
first letter S

explanation.surface: Someone living in Belgrade foresees industrial action coming from the east.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letters give BRES; reading them from the east, right to left, gives the answer, which also describes a Belgrade resident.
explanation.definitionFit: Belgrade is the capital of Serbia, so a person living there is typically a Serbian.

clue.text: Cruel art, cannily contrived

indicators.note: contrived means artificially put together, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A piece of art that is harsh, shrewdly put together.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyrannical ruler behaves with oppressive cruelty, like a despot.

clue.text: Politician's marriage starts to invite salacious tittle-tattle

parts.note: a union is a marriage

indicators.note: starts to means taking the first letter of each of the next three words

parts.note: first letter I
first letter S
first letter T

explanation.surface: A politician's wedding is bound to attract juicy gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: In UK politics a Unionist supports keeping the union of Northern Ireland, or Scotland, with Great Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A Unionist is a member of a party committed to preserving a political union, especially in Northern Ireland.

clue.text: Easy in Oman to develop oil- based product

indicators.note: to develop means to evolve into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Oman finds it simple to grow a petroleum industry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oil-based product' suggests petroleum, fitting Oman, but the oil here is the vegetable oil in a dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayonnaise is an emulsion of oil, egg yolk and vinegar, so it is a sauce made largely from oil.

clue.text: Solver will, reportedly, record Something for Christmas

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the spoken form is spelt differently

parts.note: the solver is you, so solver will is you'll
a log is a record, as in a ship's log

explanation.surface: The solver is told they will record something festive.
explanation.walkthrough: YOU'LL said aloud sounds like YULE, the old word for Christmas; add LOG.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yule log is a log burned at Christmas, or a chocolate log cake eaten then.

clue.text: Priceless international centres

parts.note: FOC stands for free of charge, which is without a price

explanation.surface: Valuable worldwide hubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Priceless' suggests great value, but it means costing nothing: FOC, free of charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Foci is the plural of focus, a central point of attention or activity.

clue.text: Outdoor championship just beginning late

parts.note: an Open is a championship anyone may enter, like the Open in golf

indicators.note: beginning late means the first letter is lost

parts.note: fair means just

explanation.surface: An outdoor tournament has just started behind schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just beginning' looks like a phrase, but 'just' is FAIR, and 'beginning late' removes its F.
explanation.definitionFit: Open-air means out of doors, in the open air rather than inside a building.

clue.text: Joint mostly had for starter in meal

indicators.note: for starter in means the first letter is replaced

parts.note: lunch is a meal

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: taken as written before losing its last letter

explanation.surface: Most of a roast joint was eaten as a starter at dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: HA (most of 'had') replaces L, the first letter of LUNCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A haunch is the hip and thigh, also a joint of meat such as a haunch of venison.

clue.text: He defended part of Channel so notably

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A naval hero is praised for guarding a stretch of the English Channel so well.
explanation.definitionFit: Admiral Horatio Nelson protected Britain against Napoleon's fleets, so he defended the nation at sea.

clue.text: Guide visiting Tehran destroyed holy site

indicators.note: visiting means staying inside, so the guide goes within the other letters
destroyed means broken up, so the letters of Tehran are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as the letters to rearrange
an A to Z is a British street-map guide book, written A-Z

explanation.surface: A tour guide in Iran's capital wrecked a sacred place.
explanation.walkthrough: An A-Z is the British name for a street atlas of a city, so 'Guide' is a book, not a person showing tourists round.
explanation.definitionFit: Nazareth in Galilee was the hometown of Jesus and is a place of Christian pilgrimage.

clue.text: Spirit shown by revolutionary failing to use loaf? The opposite

indicators.note: failing to use means leaving out, so these letters are dropped
the opposite says the roles are swapped: it is the loaf that fails to use the revolutionary

parts.note: a brioche is a sweet bread loaf
Che Guevara was the Argentine-born revolutionary

explanation.surface: A revolutionary, too dim to use his loaf, shows spirit; or rather the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'use loaf' is slang for think. 'The opposite' swaps the roles: the loaf, BRIOCHE, drops the revolutionary, CHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Brio means vigour and liveliness, a spirited energy in performance.

clue.text: One infiltrating to join smallest army unit

indicators.note: infiltrating means getting inside, so one goes within the other word

parts.note: to solder is to join metal with molten alloy
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A spy sneaks in to enlist in a tiny military detachment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One infiltrating to join' reads like a spy enlisting, but it is I inside SOLDER.
explanation.definitionFit: A single soldier is the smallest possible component of an army, one fighting person.

clue.text: How much is known, for example, about entertaining North Africans?

parts.note: ken means range of knowledge, as in beyond my ken

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so North goes inside the reversed word
about means turned around, so say is read backwards

parts.note: say is used to mean for example

explanation.surface: A question about how much is understood regarding North Africans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North' looks like part of the definition, but Kenya is in East Africa; North is just the N inside YAS (SAY reversed).
explanation.definitionFit: Kenyans are people from Kenya, a country in East Africa.

clue.text: Nameless bloke organised meeting

indicators.note: nameless means the abbreviation N for name is removed

parts.note: a gent is a man or bloke
a together person is well organised

explanation.surface: An anonymous man arranged a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' looks like an anagram signal, but it is the colloquial TOGETHER; GENT loses N (name) to give GET.
explanation.definitionFit: A get-together is an informal social gathering of friends or colleagues.
